challenges.title: Website
challenges.summary: An open website brief: the model invents the subject, brand, content and visual direction of a complete site.
challenges.requirement: Original concept and identity; substantial real content; responsive layout; working interactions; accessible and fast

challenges.title: Production Site Refresh
challenges.summary: A fixed source: refresh the live Shutterhaus Visuals production site — same doctrine, a generation better, shipped as one self-contained static folder.
challenges.requirement: All five public pages rebuilt; keyboard gallery and scroll frames preserved; zero third-party requests; no build step; content in the markup; WCAG 2.2 AA; verified performance budget

challenges.title: Restaurant Website
challenges.summary: A restaurant or cafe website with a full menu, reservations and a distinctive art direction.
challenges.requirement: Real menu with 30+ items; reservation and order flows with validation; opening-hours logic; strong identity; responsive and accessible

challenges.title: Editorial Website
challenges.summary: A complete editorial publication with a distinctive identity, substantial content and a considered multi-page reading experience.
challenges.requirement: Semantic HTML; sophisticated CSS layout and typography; homepage plus two content pages; responsive navigation; accessible and polished

challenges.title: CSS Interactive Experience
challenges.summary: An original interactive browser experience built with HTML and advanced CSS, without JavaScript.
challenges.requirement: CSS-only interaction and animation; advanced layout and custom properties; responsive states; reduced-motion support; accessible native controls

challenges.title: Design System
challenges.summary: A complete reusable design system with tokens, components, variants and a showcase of the system in use.
challenges.requirement: Semantic HTML and CSS; coherent design tokens; reusable components; interaction states; responsive showcase; accessible component patterns

challenges.title: JavaScript Application
challenges.summary: A complete browser application built with vanilla JavaScript, meaningful workflows and persistent user data.
challenges.requirement: Vanilla JavaScript; real state and data management; multiple views; validation and error handling; persistence; import/export where relevant

challenges.title: Three.js 3D Experience
challenges.summary: An original interactive 3D browser experience built around a real Three.js scene.
challenges.requirement: Three.js rendering; geometry, materials and lighting; camera and scene interaction; animation; responsive controls; performance and WebGL fallback

challenges.title: SVG Drawing Studio
challenges.summary: A browser-based vector drawing studio where users create, select, transform and export real SVG artwork.
challenges.requirement: SVG-first rendering; editable shapes and paths; selection and transforms; fill and stroke controls; undo/redo; SVG export; pointer and keyboard support

challenges.title: Creative Tool
challenges.summary: A professional-grade creative tool in the browser: layered, non-destructive, fast and dense enough for real work.
challenges.requirement: Real file open and export; layered non-destructive workflow with undo/redo; eight or more tools; autosave; smooth zoom and pan on large canvases

challenges.title: Generative Art
challenges.summary: A seeded generative artwork that evolves in real time and is worth watching rather than a screensaver.
challenges.requirement: Deterministic seeding from the URL; three or more scenes or developments; collaborative interaction; high-resolution PNG export; adaptive resolution

challenges.title: Browser Operating System
challenges.summary: A complete desktop operating system in the browser with its own identity, window management and a shared filesystem.
challenges.requirement: Window manager with snap and z-order; persisted shared filesystem; eight or more apps including a terminal and editor; launcher search; persistent settings

challenges.title: Data Story
challenges.summary: An interactive data-driven story built on a generated dataset, told through linked custom visualisations.
challenges.requirement: Four or more hand-built visual forms with linked interaction; a genuine insight with a narrative arc; annotations, tooltips and CSV export; responsive redraw

runs.notes: A monochrome generative-art gallery site: animated hero flow-field canvas, six seeded procedural artworks (ridgelines, harmonograph, moire, halftone bloom, ordered dither, paper weave) with re-run and expand controls, an interactive halftone lab with contrast/gamma/cell/angle/pattern controls and working PNG export, manifesto, colophon and footer. Vanilla HTML/CSS/JS, zero dependencies, relative paths, works from file:// and GitHub Pages. Known limitations: system font stacks only (no webfont files, to stay dependency-free); artwork appearance varies by seed since every image is generated at run time; canvases require JavaScript.
runs.title: Mono®

runs.notes: PENUMBRA — a single-page monochrome exhibition of six generative artworks, all drawn at runtime with Canvas 2D from seeded value-noise and an ordered-dither pass; no image files, no external dependencies, no build step. Each work opens into a dialog with live controls (seed, scale, contrast, invert) and PNG export. Includes a keyboard-operable eleven-value grey scale, a scroll-progress rule, scroll reveals, a permanently fixed difference-blend header, and full prefers-reduced-motion, focus-visible, print and noscript fallbacks. Known limitations: the hero dot field animates only while visible and is capped near 30fps, so lower-power devices may drop frames; the serif and grotesque are system-font stacks, so letterforms shift slightly between platforms; the difference-blend header can lose contrast over mid-grey artwork frames.
runs.title: Penumbra

runs.notes: The Quiet Index: a monochrome editorial field guide to silence with an interactive anechoic-chamber diagram, a seven-entry ledger and a draggable decibel scale. Single static page, no dependencies or external assets. Known limitation: the generated Web Audio tone is intentionally minimal and requires a user gesture.
runs.title: The Quiet Index

runs.notes: VERDIGRIS, an invented oyster bar and Atlantic wine house in Saint-Malo intra-muros, built as one self-contained HTML file with inline CSS, JS, SVG illustration and Web Audio sound. 52 dishes, wines and cocktails with descriptions, prices and dietary markers; instant search plus category and dietary filters; a live open/closed status computed from real weekly hours and special holiday services; a custom calendar reservation flow with party-size-aware deterministic availability, inline validation, confirmation, .ics download and cancellation; a takeaway basket ('Le Comptoir') with quantities, collection slots, totals and localStorage persistence. Table availability is simulated deterministically (no backend) and all state is local to the browser; every storage access is guarded. Google Fonts (Fraunces, Archivo, DM Mono) is the only external request, with local fallback stacks, so the page also works offline. Responsive down to 360px, keyboard operable, focus-trapped overlays, reduced-motion support, DPR-aware canvas. Known limitations: no real payment or email delivery, and opening hours are fictional.
runs.title: Marrow & Tide
runs.description: A wood-fired kitchen on the coast of Maine.

runs.notes: GRAIN is a fictional monochrome film laboratory website built as a static, dependency-free single-page experience. It includes original SVG artwork, a canvas-based interactive grain simulator, accessible navigation/filter/form behaviors, and responsive editorial layout. Limitations: the contact form is client-side only (no backend submission), the mailto address uses an .example domain, and canvas grain rendering is randomized per adjustment rather than seeded for deterministic frames.
runs.title: Grain

runs.notes: Monochrome study of paper and type built as a single static page: the pulp section, an animated type-setting press, four drawn sheets, and a papermaking timeline. All text, diagrams, motion and interactivity are inline in index.html, styles.css and js/app.js — no external files, fonts or dependencies, and the page opens from file:// and from a GitHub Pages subfolder. Known limitation: reduced motion swaps the running press for static stepped angles, and the decorative hero sheet is a flat card.
runs.title: The Press House

runs.notes: Cinder & Salt, an invented Copenhagen wood-fire and fermentation kitchen. One self-contained index.html: hand-drawn SVG wordmark, dish and hearth illustrations, a procedural ember canvas, generated Web Audio ambience, a 39-item searchable menu with dietary filters, a persistent basket with collection checkout, and a reservation flow using Copenhagen-time hours, special dates and unavailable slots. Orders and bookings are client-side only; there is no backend. Google Fonts is the sole optional external request, with a full offline fallback stack.
runs.title: Cinder & Salt
runs.description: An independent restaurant, brought to life.

runs.notes: BRASA is a single-file live-fire osteria site for a fictional Fishtown, Philadelphia restaurant. Includes a 32-item illustrated SVG menu with instant search/category/dietary filters, localStorage-backed basket with quantities and totals, reservation flow with date/party-aware unavailable slots and confirmation, real-time open/closed hours with special-hours handling, mobile nav, scroll reveals, and an interactive ember canvas. Known limitation: no real backend for reservations/orders; map and confirmations are simulated client-side.
runs.title: Brasa
runs.description: An independent restaurant, brought to life.
